chapter: Later tours, illness and the union job
title: Sinus trouble on a French tour and hernia operations
summary: On a tour with Jo Jones, Milt Buckner and T-Bone Walker he lost feeling in his face, went home, and then needed hernia operations.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Anyway, I played all over, all over with them. We played Switzerland, I mean Sweden, some parts of Sweden. All over Denmark. Then I went to Germany and played Hamburg and some more places. And I got a call to go to France to make a five day tour with Jo Jones, Milt Buckner, and T-Bone Walker. And I had made four days of this tour and I became ill. I had trouble with sinus.
What time of year was it?
Oh, it was about late Spring I think it was.
So you may have been, you know at the end of the Winter, you may have been a bit run down?

boy those were the hardest days of my life trying to, I just couldn't make the last day. I made four and I had to leave because I didn't have any sensation on one side of my face at all. So I went back to France or rather I went back to Limoges France to a clinic and then I came home. Stayed two or three days then caught another plane and went right back to Switzerland again.

Because the doctors in Switzerland told me to come home, I mean in France, told me to come home right away to a doctor. And I came home and I went to an eye, ear and nose doctor who is here on 2nd Avenue. But I still had this date in Switzerland.
Now, I can feel everything here, I could feel my face again.
On the right, on the left hand side?

Yes. I could feel it. So I figured I could make this thing in Switzerland which I did. But after I got up there, after I got through with that Swiss date, I came home and I didn't, I had so many other things to go through.

Medical things, that I just didn't bother to play too much. Because I had to go for Hernia operations and that cuts you out a long time just waiting, you know. So that's the way it is up until that point.
